sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's young, mobile-first population drives sustained e-commerce and digital payment adoption, with platforms like Bukalapak capturing offline-to-online retail migration.
Government push for digital infrastructure and financial inclusion, including QRIS and digital banking licenses, creates durable demand for fintech and SaaS providers.
Local tech valuations remain attractive vs US peers, with lower correlation to global rate cycles, offering a buffer against developed market volatility.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector shows relative strength vs US, with local names like MLPT and BUKA surging on domestic digital adoption tailwinds. Favor selective exposure to e-commerce and fintech plays, as structural growth in underpenetrated markets offsets global rate headwinds.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: Domestic Indonesian banks are gaining traction as investors shift from US-listed financials, driven by improving local loan growth and stable NIMs.
Regulatory tailwinds from OJK's digital banking push and BI's accommodative policy support smaller lenders like SMIL and BPFI over larger peers.
Structural under-penetration of credit in Indonesia, with loan-to-GDP below 40%, provides durable growth runway for financials, especially in consumer and MSME segments.
sectors.ai: Indonesia financials lagged US peers but select movers like SMIL (+10.6%) and BPFI (+6.4%) signal rotation into undervalued domestic lenders. Prioritize exposure to SMIL and BPFI for near-term alpha, while trimming US-listed financials like NDAQ given relative weakness.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export demand remains structurally supported by Asian industrial growth and domestic energy needs, driving consistent volume for majors like BUMI and COAL.
Government push for downstream processing and renewable energy integration creates durable catalysts for nickel and copper plays, benefiting firms like DEWA and CUAN.
Infrastructure spending under the new administration sustains demand for construction materials and energy, underpinning gains in logistics-linked miners like ALKA and SUNI.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's mining & energy sector shows strong local momentum (+0.80%) versus US weakness, signaling domestic demand resilience. Key movers like ALKA, COAL, and BUMI highlight investor focus on coal and infrastructure-linked plays. Position into high-volume names like MEDC and CUAN for near-term upside, as normal signal suggests no systemic risk.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandatory biodiesel blending (B35) and upcoming B40 mandate create durable demand for palm-oil-based renewable fuels, directly benefiting local producers like ARKO and ESSA.
The government's 2025-2030 RUPTL (electricity supply plan) prioritizes 20GW of new renewable capacity, providing a multi-year project pipeline for developers like CDIA and PKPK.

Falling solar and battery storage costs are making Indonesia's off-grid mining and industrial electrification projects economically viable, driving structural growth for climate-tech firms like BATR a
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows resilient outperformance vs US peers, driven by domestic policy tailwinds and strong project pipelines. Focus on ARKO and 373220 as momentum leaders; their gains signal accelerating capital flows into local clean energy plays. Maintain overweight on Indonesian climate-tech, as structural demand from industrial electrification and government mandates outweighs global rate headwinds.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class income and urbanization sustain premium FMCG demand, insulating Indonesia from global slowdowns.
Government subsidies and stable rupiah support household purchasing power, benefiting mass-market consumer goods.
E-commerce penetration growth expands distribution for local brands, enabling faster market share gains against multinationals.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector shows resilience with a +0.48% gain, contrasting US weakness, driven by strong domestic demand and lower input costs. Key movers like AGAR and ZATA signal robust local consumption, making selective exposure to staples and discretionary names attractive for near-term alpha.

themes: Indonesia's mandatory health insurance (JKN) expansion is structurally boosting volume for diagnostic and hospital service providers like RLCO, as coverage drives more formal-sector patient visits.
Aging demographics and rising chronic disease prevalence in Indonesia create durable demand for specialized healthcare services, benefiting firms with laboratory and diagnostic capabilities.

Government push for domestic medical equipment manufacturing and digital health integration supports long-term margins for local players, reducing import dependency and improving service accessibility
sectors.ai: Buy RLCO on its +13.50% breakout as Indonesia's expanding private hospital network drives demand for diagnostic and lab services, mirroring global trends; TMO and DGX gains confirm the subsector's momentum, with RLCO's local scale offering direct exposure to rising medical tourism and middle-class healthcare spending.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: E-commerce expansion in Indonesia continues to drive last-mile delivery demand, benefiting logistics firms like SOCI and TAXI with higher parcel volumes.
Government infrastructure spending on toll roads and ports reduces transit costs, structurally improving margins for operators like HATM and PPGL.
Rising manufacturing and commodity exports from Indonesia's resource sector boost freight demand, supporting specialized logistics providers such as TAMU and LOPI.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's logistics sector shows strong local outperformance (+1.27% vs US -0.83%), driven by sharp gains in SOCI (+11.28%) and TAMU (+10.00%), signaling robust domestic demand. Watch for sustained momentum as e-commerce and infrastructure projects fuel volume growth, but remain cautious on global headwinds.

sectors.name: Entertainment, Media & Consumer Services
themes: Rising middle-class disposable income in Indonesia is driving premium content consumption and live entertainment spending, benefiting companies like ENAK and MDIA.
Digital advertising and out-of-home media are gaining share from traditional channels, supported by urbanization and smartphone penetration, boosting VIVA and DOOH.
Consolidation in the media space, with FUTR and FORE expanding via M&A, is creating scale efficiencies and pricing power in a fragmented market.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's entertainment and media sector is showing strong local momentum, with FUTR, ENAK, and MDIA surging on domestic demand. Focus on structural tailwinds from rising digital ad spend and content consumption, while US weakness offers a contrarian entry. Position in VIVA and DOOH for ad recovery and out-of-home growth.

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate
themes: Jakarta's new capital city (IKN) construction is driving land-banking and infrastructure-linked property plays, benefiting developers with Kalimantan exposure like TAMA and KOTA.
The government's housing subsidy program (FLPP) continues to support affordable housing demand, insulating mid-tier developers from rate hike sensitivity.
Urbanization and rising middle-class consumption in secondary cities (e.g., Medan, Makassar) are creating durable demand for mixed-use developments, favoring diversified players like MANG and GRIA.
sectors.ai: Indonesia property sector shows selective strength with small-cap names surging, but aggregate modest gain suggests rotation into laggards rather than broad re-rating. Watch for sustained volume confirmation on movers like MPRO and WINR before committing capital; US property weakness adds caution.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Regulatory tailwinds from OJK's sandbox framework are driving institutional adoption of compliant stablecoins and tokenized assets in Indonesia.
Retail speculative demand, fueled by rising digital asset awareness and low entry barriers, amplifies volatility in small-cap tokens like BCAP and BEAT.
Global macro liquidity shifts, particularly US rate expectations, directly impact Indonesian crypto flows, with stablecoins acting as a safe-haven proxy for local investors.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's crypto sector is surging on global momentum, with BCAP's explosive 363% gain signaling speculative frenzy. Prioritize exposure to stablecoin-linked assets like STABLE and USTB for yield, while monitoring regulatory clarity from OJK—this rally is fragile and rotation into quality is imminent.
